messages:
Maya: FYI we saw a regression tied to the deploy-time warmers on model x-2 during the autoscale event a few minutes ago. KV hit-rate tanked and tail latency spiked. digging in now :face_with_monocle:
deploy-bot: deploy started: release/2026-03-18-1530 (model x-2) :rocket:
Maya: quick profiler snapshot:
```
2026-03-18T15:31:02Z warmers: synthetic rate=500 qps
KV_hit_rate: baseline=78% current=34%
P95_token_latency: baseline=42ms current=180ms
GPU_util: baseline=71% current=92%
KV_evictions/s: baseline=12 current=140
```
Ben: ouch. that eviction/s bump is huge. are the warmers generating high cardinality keys? can you paste a sample of the warm payloads?
Maya: copying an anonymized request we used for the prefill job: `{"prompt": "<user_prefix>#session/abc123#... long user context ..."}`. note the session id and ephemeral tokens are included in the hash right now.
Chris: that will do it. if key = full prompt hash and warmers include session ids, you get near-zero reuse and you end up thrashing the KV. plus the new kernel selection (v3-kv-compact) packed keys differently so evictions are more likely under the same memory pressure.
Tia: kernel note: kernel v3 changed the in-memory layout to be denser but has a slightly higher eviction cost when map entropy increases. we saw small perf wins for steady-state but worse behavior under synthetic high-cardinality traffic. recommend gating warmers by kernel.
Sasha: agree. two quick ideas: 1) normalize keying for warmers (strip session ids / hash only first N tokens), 2) change warmers from burst 500qps -> staged ramp 10->100qps. start an AB to compare. :+1:
Ben: can we get a KV key histogram and top-1k keys captured from the warmers window? that will prove high-cardinality source.
Maya: uploaded a sample to s3://redwood/profiles/2934567800/warm_keys_sample.txt — shows ~92% unique keys across warm requests.
Chris: config suggestion to normalize keying (pseudo-yaml):
```
warmers:
  keying:
    mode: prefix_normalize
    keep_tokens: 128   # only use first 128 tokens for cache key
    strip_patterns: ["session/.*", "user_id:.*"]
  rate: 50qps
  ramp: 10->50 over 60s
  selector:
    kernel_exclude: ["v3-kv-compact"]
```
Tia: also propose adding a per-node warmer circuit breaker: if KV_evictions/s > 50 for 3 consecutive minutes, scale warmers down on that node or stop them. reduces blast radius.
Sasha: I'll spin up two scheduled jobs for the AB: A (ramped low-card warmers + prefix_normalize) vs B (current warmers) for the next 6h window then collect hit-rate + p95 + evictions. cron we'll use: 
```
# run every 5m, ramp 10->100 qps over 30s (A)
*/5 * * * * /opt/prewarm --model x-2 --mode ramp --min-qps 10 --max-qps 100 --ramp-duration 30s --keying prefix_normalize --keep 128
# control (B) uses existing burst config at 500 qps
```
Ben: make sure to attach a perf profile (perf, nvprof) and heap snapshot at start/end of each job. also collect kernel id for each node so we can correlate with kernel selection.
Maya: switched warmers off on the most affected fleet (temp) — disabled prefill job id=pf-2934567. early numbers are already better: KV_hit_rate creeping back to 65% and P95 down to ~60ms. will continue to monitor. :eyes:
deploy-bot: prefill job pf-2934567 disabled by Maya at 2026-03-18T15:33:12Z
Chris: long-term we should add key normalization helpers into the runtime so any prefill/prefetch tooling can call a shared normalizer. avoids ad-hoc logic in jobs.
Tia: I'll add the circuit-breaker and kernel exclusion flags to the warmers operator today, and add metrics for 'warm_key_cardinality' and 'warm_kv_evictions' to the console dashboards.
Sasha: running AB now (A ramped normalized vs B baseline). will push results to /dashboards/ab/2934567800 by EOD.
Ben: thanks all. action items: Sasha run AB, Tia add operator gating + metrics, Chris add normalizer CR, Maya keep monitoring + attach traces, I'll handle perf capture automation. close loop before next deploy. :white_check_mark:
